name: Open Marxism
summary: Open Marxism is a non-deterministic reading of Marx, consolidated in Britain around 1990, that treats capital, state, money and value as fetishised forms of an ongoing and indeterminate class struggle. It rejects the base/superstructure model, vanguard parties and state socialism, and looks to self-organisation, councils and refusal aimed at abolishing the state and class rather than capturing them.
scope: The British Open Marxism of Bonefeld, Gunn, Psychopedis, Holloway and the Common Sense circle, as set out in the Open Marxism volumes (1992) and Holloway's later work, with autonomist, Frankfurt and Luxemburgist influences. It excludes structuralist, analytical and party-state Marxism, which it calls closed. Most social, cultural and foreign-policy statements are outside what the texts discuss, so those answers are inferences from the core principles.

keyFigures.name: John Holloway
keyFigures.role: Open Marxist theorist of fetishism, class composition and refusal; author of Change the World Without Taking Power.

keyFigures.name: Werner Bonefeld
keyFigures.role: Co-editor of the Open Marxism volumes and theorist of the state as a form of capital.

sources.title: Open Marxism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview, key thinkers, and positions on the state, party, class, base/superstructure and state socialism.

sources.title: Social constitution and the form of the capitalist state
sources.author: Werner Bonefeld (Open Marxism vol. 1, 1992)
sources.usedFor: The state as moment of class antagonism, rights as forms of exploitation, rejection of objective laws and crisis theory.

sources.title: Open Marxism 2: Theory and Practice, editors introduction
sources.author: Bonefeld, Gunn, Psychopedis (eds.)
sources.usedFor: Unity of theory and practice, rejection of determinism and scientism, capital as recomposing itself.

sources.title: Debate between John Holloway and Alex Callinicos: Can we change the world without taking power?
sources.author: John Holloway, Alex Callinicos (World Social Forum)
sources.usedFor: Holloway on the state, party, revolution now, direct democracy and the citizen/foreigner distinction.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; an anti-capitalist current would back decommodified care, though it distrusts the state as its provider, hence only mild agreement inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Bonefeld treats welfare-state gains as struggle-won but integrating; adherents would support the wage fight yet see reform as accommodation, so they split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Value, money and the market are treated as fetishised forms of the capital-labour antagonism, so claims for market efficiency are what the critique targets.

public-ownership.rationale: Open Marxism criticises the "statist myth of socialism"; nationalisation swaps one state-capital form for another, so adherents disagree despite being anti-capitalist.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources do not discuss taxation; redistribution through the state is both welcome as a gain and dismissed as reformist integration.

unions-good.rationale: Workers' self-organisation is central, but unions as institutions often channel struggle into capital's terms; inferred mild support.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bonefeld argues property rights are the juridical form through which exploitation is secured, so treating them as fundamental is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is a state-form compromise within capital; adherents see it as neither a goal nor worthless, with no stated position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is a product of past class struggle in Bonefeld's account; cutting it is austerity against labour, though adherents also critique welfare's disciplining role.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-determination of work is central, but ownership of firms within a market is not the aim; abolition of the value form is, so only mild support inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from hostility to the state as an instrument of domination and the emphasis on autonomy; no source discusses terrorism or surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from libertarian anti-state, anti-discipline stance of autonomist-influenced theory.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents distrust handing the state coercive power, though they oppose racism, so inferred weak disagreement.

strong-leader.rationale: The article rejects the vanguard as reproducing leader/led hierarchy and favours self-organisation, which extends against strong-leader rule.

state-harmful.rationale: The state is held to be a political form of capitalist social relations and the aim is its abolition rather than seizure; "harmful" is inferred from that.

limit-guns.rationale: No source addresses gun control; adherents are anti-state yet not pro-gun as such, so genuinely unstated.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and military belong to the state form that secures capital's rule; strengthening them runs against the abolition aim.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between decriminalisation and treating it as commodified labour.

decide-locally.rationale: Favours autonomous self-organisation from below such as assemblies and communes, so local decision is mildly favoured over national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from view that crime and punishment are products of social relations rather than individual defects.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; critique of social forms and unpaid reproductive work from Dalla Costa influence implies scepticism of the traditional family as foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory orientation, though marriage as state institution is viewed critically.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory, autonomy-centred outlook.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from materialist critique, with no stated stance on public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory orientation, with the caveat that race and class are not separated in a single-antagonism theory.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the view that social categories are historically constituted forms rather than natural facts.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; national states are treated as moments of the world market and the stance is internationalist, so national culture is no priority.

gradual-change.rationale: Holloway demands "revolution here and now" rather than waiting for the right time, and rejects respect for the state as organisational form.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Holloway criticises the state's distinction between citizens and foreigners, so restriction is disfavoured.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; international institutions are state forms in the world market, so more power for them is unlikely to be welcomed.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed directly; free trade is a market form of capital, and the critique of political economy rejects the claim that it benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: Bonefeld places national economies within the world market and the stance is internationalist, so national interest above cooperation is rejected.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to states as instruments of domination, so military action by states is doubted.

open-borders.rationale: Holloway criticises the state's citizen/foreigner line; open borders is inferred as consistent, though never stated as a demand.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; critique of capital's endless valorisation points toward limits, but adherents do not state an environmental programme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; support for action is likely but doubt that capitalist states can deliver it, so the answer is unstated and split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Rejects scientism and positivism; technological fixes within capital are viewed as forms of its domination rather than solutions.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No source touches energy policy and no principle decides it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Holloway insists on revolution here and now and the article treats refusal and revolution as the core of theory and practice.

experts-over-public.rationale: Theory is a critical practice rather than a scientific guide applied from outside; the rejection of external expert direction extends to policy.

central-planning.rationale: The "statist myth of socialism" and state Marxism are rejected as reproducing fetishism, so central planning is not the alternative to markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market categories like value and money are forms of capital, so worker-owned markets are not the goal, though the sources never judge this specific model.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxation reform is not discussed and no principle settles it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; a redistributive reform that adherents neither prioritise nor oppose.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; may be seen as a gain against capital or as a state integration device, so adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: National protection frames workers as part of national capital; the world-market, internationalist view suggests disagreement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy reproduces the statist form that is criticised, so it is disfavoured.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is understood as a form of exploitation, so spreading it is not a solution; not discussed explicitly.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Class abolition and the critique of value, money and the labour economy aim at ending capitalist forms; Holloway frames struggle as against labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would reject market money as much as state money, so they reject the premise of this statement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Binding capital and labour into state bodies is class integration, the opposite of autonomous struggle.

one-party-rule.rationale: The article states the vanguard party is a bourgeois form reproducing hierarchy, and state-Marxist rule is criticised as closed Marxism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; hereditary rule conflicts with the anti-hierarchy, self-determination commitments.

democracy-best.rationale: Holloway rejects representative democracy for direct democracy, so adherents split on democracy as a general form of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Holloway opposes representative democracy and favours "some form of direct democracy," though through assemblies rather than referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: The article cites workers' councils, assemblies and communes as the preferred autonomous forms of organisation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination is favoured but nation-building is not.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; strongly against by egalitarian, anti-hierarchy logic.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolution is defended and refusal is central, but no source endorses violence, so disagreement is mild.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalism and critique of nationalism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from materialist and anti-state views.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the critique of state law as a form of capital and from the secular materialism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private security is capital's own rule exercised without a state, so it is rejected even more than public provision.

military-superiority.rationale: Militarism is a function of states within the world market, and the stance is internationalist and anti-state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Internationalist stance and critique of national forms make ethnic homogeneity unwelcome; not explicitly discussed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bonefeld states that history is the history of class struggle and structures are modes of existence of class antagonism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Class abolition implies equality, but adherents avoid distributive formulas centred on the state, so mild agreement.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Zapatismo is cited approvingly as autonomous self-organisation, which implies support for indigenous autonomy; the specific claim is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; support in principle but reparations are a state-to-state mechanism, so unstated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; supranational blocs defined by religion or civilization conflict with class internationalism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The critique of capitalist society targets the atomised individual of bourgeois form; self-interest as a moral good is rejected.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Formal rights are criticised as forms of domination, but duties to community ahead of individuals are also not endorsed; inferred disagreement.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on the value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; population limits are a state-imposed, scientistic fix, which is disfavoured.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; capital is critiqued but industrial civilization is not rejected as such.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Anti-scientism and the critique of capital's drive to revolutionise production imply scepticism toward acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources never discuss body or mind technology; adherents have no settled view and could see both emancipation and commodification in it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Technocratic algorithmic rule is the opposite of self-determination and an alienated form of state.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to state control and surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: The dialectic is open and oriented toward overcoming existing forms; restoring a past order is rejected.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Theory against society is critical; pragmatic dismissal of theory conflicts with the unity of theory and practice.

direct-action.rationale: Holloway supports revolution now in the gaps of capitalism and self-organisation over party-state politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Holloway insists on non-hierarchical self-determination now, and rejects the party as a form that already contains betrayal.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; no source holds this, and Marxist tradition values the human productive power capital creates.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not stated in the sources; the aim of abolishing labour and class implies it in Marxist terms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Classic Marxist communist principle, but the sources themselves do not state it, so inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposition to capitalist valorisation and the value form implies production for need, but this is not quoted in the sources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Bonefeld says labour is the substance of value and capital exists only through living labour, so profit comes from exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Aim is abolition of state and classes, with workers' councils and communes, not a party-state dictatorship; "dictatorial power" is disfavoured.

collective-farming.rationale: No source discusses agriculture; the anti-statist stress on voluntary self-organisation cuts against both compulsion and collective mandates, so it is left split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; imperialism theory is not a distinctive Open Marxist theme, which stresses open class struggle over inevitability.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject the premise of a natural private-property entitlement.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberal limits on the state are seen as fetishised forms, so only mild disagreement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are criticised as forms of bourgeois society; collective subjects are not denied.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; state coercion into the military conflicts with anti-state commitments.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; focus is on collective self-organisation, not individual exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers is a market logic that is the target of critique.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not stated; formal freedom is a form of domination in Bonefeld, implying freedom needs material substance.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; power is located in capitalist social relations rather than in cultural elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; rejects naturalised social categories and positivism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation integrates classes under the state, which is opposed.

total-state.rationale: The state is the political form of capital and its abolition is the aim; state direction of all life is the opposite.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist myths are alien to an internationalist critique.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; imperial expansion is opposed by the internationalist stance.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; feudal hierarchy conflicts with the egalitarian orientation.

bound-labor.rationale: Not addressed; unfree labour contradicts self-determination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Theory is rejected as neutral, positivist science; theory is a critical practice and "theory against society."

universal-morality.rationale: Anti-positivist; moral truths known by reason across cultures are doubted, but the sources do not discuss them.

single-common-good.rationale: The antagonism between capital and labour denies a single common good in capitalist society.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; nation-state projects are viewed as capitalist state forms.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources say nothing on diaspora or citizenship rules; the critique of state citizenship pulls one way and solidarity with the displaced the other.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nation-building project the sources never take up; adherents are indifferent to it as such.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Support for self-organisation of workers' councils and assemblies suggests agreement, though within capitalism it is a limited reform.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-based public provision is a commodity form; not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; austerity is opposed as an attack on labour in the crisis.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom in the market sense is a fetishised form of exploitation; political freedom is not founded on it.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; moral hierarchy by rulers conflicts with self-determination.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination is valued for working people, not nations or states, which are forms of capital.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; state military force is disfavoured.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-positivism and "reconstructed" Hegel mean a non-scientistic reason; stance on faith is not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Holloway criticises the citizen/foreigner distinction as the state's logic; excluding immigrants from welfare is rejected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Holloway frames struggle against labour; compulsory work disciplines labour for capital.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class is an antagonistic relation and the aim is abolishing classes; class partnership is the integration being critiqued.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; no support for futurist destruction of culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; anti-imperialism is a concern but state fronts are not endorsed.

workers-nation.rationale: Class is internationalist; Bonefeld places the state within the world market, so national organisation of workers is rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emancipatory outlook.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; interest is part of capital's forms but legal bans are statist.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; fully opposed by egalitarian logic.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The article explicitly rejects the state as a neutral tool; Bonefeld calls it a moment of the class antagonism, not an instrument external to capital.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; only inferred scepticism of capital's accumulation drive.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; critique of the state's national logic.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory incompatible with form analysis that locates domination in social relations.

proportional-representation.rationale: Parliamentary electoral design is outside the concern of an anti-parliamentary stance.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; national mission is alien to internationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Influences include Dalla Costa; structural domination by gender is plausible but not explicitly stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; critique is of the state form, not individual corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; eugenics fully opposed by egalitarian logic.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; mild support from critique of state violence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Opposes liberal state as protector of property relations.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Never addressed, but an anti-racist, emancipatory theory would reject state or social pressure against mixed marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formal equality is critiqued as a form masking exploitation, but equal worth is assumed in the emancipatory aim, so mild agreement.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; internationalism favoured but doctrine not a theme.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources never discuss settler colonialism, and adherents' class-centred framing leaves the classification open.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law reform is not discussed; a critique of state law as a capital form leaves adherents without a clear stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; state restriction of belief disfavoured.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; religious state law is disfavoured.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; secular materialism is assumed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Open Marxism rejects state socialism and its aim is abolition of the state, so a strengthening socialist state is rejected.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not addressed; social-contract legitimacy is a bourgeois form.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export drives treat the national economy as a competitor in the world market, a framing that Bonefeld's world-market analysis does not endorse; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority is state coercion against people and is inferred to be rejected under internationalist egalitarianism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian absolutism is alien to class analysis.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition is capital's mode of discipline, not a source of progress for the critique.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; state suppression of parties is disfavoured.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; domination is the core concept, though republican reform of the state is not the aim.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; separation of the political is a fetishised form.

vanguard-party.rationale: The article states Open Marxism criticises the vanguard party as bourgeois form reproducing leader/led hierarchy and disciplining struggle.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from the stress on labour's side in class antagonism; adherents would back the poor's needs but not as a state-delivered programme.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing privatisation is a policy question the sources never address, and it divides adherents between tenant interests and decommodified housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour struggle is central, so legal restriction is opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is caused by social relations of capital, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The claim is not discussed; internationalism and the view that social divisions arise from class relations lead adherents to reject it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to representative politics may incline to it but not stated.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency repression by the state is inferred to be rejected given the view of the state as a form of domination over labour.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could see price controls as a gain won against capital or as an administrative management of the market.

party-controls-media.rationale: The article's opposition to party-state hierarchy and its call for autonomy imply rejection of party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of armed forces is the state-socialist model that the article criticises along with vanguard parties and state Marxism.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with anti-hierarchy but limited to reform.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline reproduces hierarchy per the article.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU is a state form of capital; not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the military is a state-power question the sources skip; inferred rejection from anti-state and anti-hierarchy commitments.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is never addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the general hostility to hierarchical authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is not discussed; it is inferred to be rejected on materialist and anti-hierarchy grounds.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Internationalist heritage via Luxemburg, but not stated in the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship is not discussed; state moral policing is inferred to conflict with autonomy and critical theory.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Electoral term rules belong to the parliamentary politics that adherents regard as secondary; inferred mild disagreement with entrenching rulers.

recall-officials.rationale: Holloway supports direct democracy; recall is consistent but not stated.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed; adherents oppose militarism but treat any state's foreign policy as a capital form.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mandatory home ownership is a property-owner model that sits poorly with a critique of property, but adherents have no stated view.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed citizenry is a historic socialist demand but is not in the sources; adherents are split between distrust of state arms and distrust of arming.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romanticising rural life is not part of the sources' concerns; inferred mild disagreement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a state-building aim the sources do not take up; internationalism makes adherents cool toward it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are largely academic and opposed to anti-intellectualism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emancipatory, anti-hierarchical outlook.

death-penalty.rationale: Never discussed; state killing is inferred to be rejected given the view of the state as a form of domination.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild support from the emancipatory orientation, with the state school's role viewed critically.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The sources never discuss it; a materialist, critical outlook is inferred to reject it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would be torn between anti-censorship and critique of commodified sexuality.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed, but the critique of the state's citizen/foreigner distinction suggests rejecting descent-based exclusion.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild support for the autonomy of minorities.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no settled view on legal exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred mild agreement from the anti-conformist, autonomy-centred outlook.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed directly; inferred mild agreement from opposition to austerity against labour and to the discipline of capital.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political forms are tied to economic forms, so political independence alone is insufficient; inferred from form analysis.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making is a state-form matter the sources skip; adherents favour assemblies from below but not constitutional design as such.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmentalist dictatorship contradicts the emphasis on self-determination and the critique of state-led accumulation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is a state-to-state mechanism the sources never discuss; adherents have no settled view.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are a state power instrument; inferred rejection from anti-militarism and anti-state commitments.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election design is outside the concerns of the sources; no clear stance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not discussed; independence insulates money from democratic pressure, which adherents would regard as a fetishised form, inferred mild disagreement.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are not discussed; internationalists lean toward not treating land as a national possession.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is tied to exploitation, not justified by common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The article's critique of the "statist myth of socialism" and state Marxism implies the USSR reproduced capital.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The sources are silent on environmental regulation; adherents are neither for nor against by principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; military alliances are state forms.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not discussed; adherents give no stated view on annexation law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would be wary of empowering the state against religion as of religious power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state symbolism is not discussed; the unifying-symbol notion is inferred to be disfavoured.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: State military force against regions is inferred to be rejected given the anti-state stance.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view on special-status regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship is inferred to be rejected on materialist and anti-hierarchy grounds.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not discussed; a regressive-leaning tax design is inferred mildly disfavoured from class-based views.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social relations constitute the individual; categories are practical.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule unbound by law is inferred to be rejected as an arbitrary form of domination, though law itself is criticised as capital's form.

space-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; mild disagreement inferred since it is a capital-driven expansion project, not an emancipatory goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed; inferred mild disagreement since few-and-many rule frames class rule as a constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship contradicts the article's rejection of leader/led hierarchy and stress on self-organisation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed; no settled view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class antagonism persists wherever the value form does; Open Marxism criticises state socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not discussed; adherents support land for those who work it in principle but the state-led redistribution form is doubted, so left split.

refugee-return.rationale: Not discussed; mild support inferred from the criticism of the citizen/foreigner distinction and solidarity with the displaced.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is inferred to be rejected as nationalist state-building contrary to internationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: State punishment of belief is inferred to be rejected on grounds of autonomy.

women-must-cover.rationale: State compulsion over dress is inferred to be rejected as coercive domination.

common-currency.rationale: Not discussed; money is a form of capital either way, and currency union is inferred mildly disfavoured as a state-capital arrangement.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic or linguistic political union is inferred to be rejected as alien to class internationalism.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; adherents have no stated view on minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would support solidarity and mobility, with no stated position on this strategy question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The article states Open Marxism rejects the mechanical base/superstructure model of the 1859 Preface and holds history is made by class struggle.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is a liberal-state measure to preserve competition, which the critique of capital does not treat as a goal; inferred mild disagreement.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not discussed; adherents oppose bailouts of capital but also austerity, so left split.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The school treats social categories as open and class as the main antagonism, and gives no basis for weighting a gendered outlook; inferred, not stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state and militarised power; the sources do not discuss arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Holloway's call for direct democracy and rejection of rule by state elites; diplomacy is not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Controls would be state action, which the school rejects, yet it opposes the free movement of capital; adherents would split and the sources do not say.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Bonefeld treats the state as a form of capitalist social relations, so a state monopoly on force is not something the school would defend; this is inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The school draws on Luxemburgist and council-communist anti-war traditions and refuses the state's claims on workers; refusal is inferred as welcome.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Bonefeld sees union and welfare gains as won by struggle but integrating, so adherents would back workers' collective organisation while doubting its limits.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would see top-ups as an accommodation that subsidises low wages, so they split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Bonefeld criticises state-imposed discipline of capital and austerity as forms of authoritarian liberal statecraft; binding fiscal rules are inferred to be opposed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The school is not reformist about global institutions; it would favour poorer countries' struggles but doubts that rule changes help, so it is inferred neutral.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Holloway argues for changing the world without taking power, and the school holds that the state is a form of capital relations that must be abolished and replaced by self-organised councils.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The school rejects blueprints and vanguard planning in favour of open, self-organised struggle, so pluralism of arrangements is inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The school's critique of value and commodity forms suggests it would reject pricing nature as capital; this is inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: The school aims at abolishing states and class rather than celebrating nations; an enduring sacred nation is inferred to be rejected.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Debt is treated as a mechanism of capitalist discipline, so cancellation is inferred as welcome.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not discussed; adherents attend to class relations over regional ones and also draw on autonomist and anti-colonial thinking.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The school treats human subjectivity as socially constituted and historically open, so a fixed nature as the basis of dignity is inferred to be rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; adherents would favour decommodified media but distrust the state as funder.

missingStatements.text: The laws of capitalist development are not objective necessities but the fetishised form of ongoing class struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: Bonefeld and the Open Marxism editors reject deterministic laws of capital and call them forms of the movement of class struggle.

missingStatements.text: Socialist change should aim to abolish the state rather than capture it.
missingStatements.rationale: The school holds that the state is a form of capitalist social relations so the goal is abolition, and Holloway argues for change without taking power.

notes: Open Marxists treat social categories as open and class as a negative relation to be abolished. Holloway is explicitly unsure whether power can be avoided, and Bonefeld does not call directly for abolition in the cited essay, so the anti-state answers rest on the Wikipedia account and Holloway more than on a single programme. Many answers are low-confidence inferences.
